column1: # Probe corpus for jq evaluator error-message parity (#356).
# Each row is a filter/input pair on which the pinned jq REPORTS AN ERROR.
# ./scripts/sync-jq-error-messages.sh runs jq over every row and records the
# message it prints into tests/data/jq-error-messages.tsv, which
# tests/jq_error_message_tests.rs then asserts both succinctly evaluators
# `#` lines and blank lines are ignored. <id> must be unique and is the key
# A row on which jq does NOT error is a hard error in the sync script: this
# corpus only describes error wording, so a probe that stopped erroring is
# either a bad probe or a jq behaviour change that needs a human look.
# Group order follows the message taxonomy in
# ── Indexing reached through paths, assignment, deletion, destructuring ──────
# `indices`/`index`/`rindex` index their input with the pattern, so a
# non-string pattern on a string input reports that same indexing error.
# … and an input they cannot search reports the same indexing error. `null`
# and an object with a string pattern are absent on purpose: jq answers those
# with `null`, so no probe can hold them (unit tests do).
# jq defines `from_entries` as object construction over the entries —
# `map({(.key // .Key // .name // .Name): …})` — so a non-string key is refused
# where it would be inserted, and `with_entries` and `{(f):v}` inherit the same
# sentence. Before #391 every entry below was silently dropped instead.
# No key alias at all, and an entry that is `null`, both leave the key `null`.
# The chain's *last* alias has nothing to be skipped in favour of, so a falsy
# `Name` is the key — `a // b` yields `b` whatever `b` is. The pair below is
# what separates that from a tail that is merely absent.
# A non-object entry is indexed with "key" all the same, so it reports the
# indexing error rather than this section's sentence.
# `with_entries` is `to_entries | map(f) | from_entries`, so an array input
# reaches `from_entries` with its indices as keys — and a filter that writes a
# The construction `from_entries` is defined over, reached directly.
# ── <v> has no keys / has no length / cannot be sorted / matched ─────────────
# `to_entries` is defined over `keys_unsorted`, so it borrows `keys`' refusal
# Same jq definition as `ascii_downcase`, so the same sentence — probed
